task.question: How many people are reported missing in Tibet after the floods in August 2026?
task.evidence: August 26 – 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods: At least 1,130 people are killed and nearly 4,500 reported missing in Tibet Autonomous Region after a flash flood strikes between Tibet and Nepal.

answer:
As of 16 September 2026, there were 519 people reported missing in Tibet following the floods. 

FINAL: 519

How many people are reported missing in Tibet after the floods in August 2026?

[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods] On the morning of 26 August 2026, a series of flash floods and debris flows destroyed the Gyirong Port on the China–Nepal border and struck dozens of settlements along a 72 km (45 mi) stretch of the Trishuli River in Nepal. These events are also known as the 2026 Nepal-China floods, Bhotekoshi flood, or Rasuwa flood. At least 1,455 deaths and 5,285 missing persons in Nepal, and 43 deaths and 519 missing in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China were reported. The flood carried the bodies of some victims 250 km (160 mi) away into neighbouring India. The precipitating geological event, initially reported as a glacier collapse in the Langtang region of the Himalayas, caused a chain reaction whose tremors were detected by seismometers worldwide, with magnitudes reaching Ms 5.2. According to experts at the National Society for Earthquake Technology–Nepal (NSET), the University of Reading and Newcastle University, the flood was triggered by a large rock-ice avalanche originating from the Lirung massif, involving glacier ice and rock, which transformed into a highly mobile, long-runout debris flow and generated destructive downstream flooding. | другие статьи: 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood, Weather of 2026

On the morning of 26 August 2026, a series of flash floods and debris flows destroyed the Gyirong Port on the China–Nepal border and struck dozens of settlements along a 72 km (45 mi) stretch of the Trishuli River in Nepal. These events are also known as the 2026 Nepal-China floods, Bhotekoshi flood, or Rasuwa flood.
At least 1,455 deaths and 5,285 missing persons in Nepal, and 43 deaths and 519 missing in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China were reported. The flood carried the bodies of some victims 250 km (160 mi) away into neighbouring India.
The precipitating geological event, initially reported as a glacier collapse in the Langtang region of the Himalayas, caused a chain reaction whose tremors were detected by seismometers worldwide, with magnitudes reaching Ms 5.2.
According to experts at the National Society for Earthquake Technology–Nepal (NSET), the University of Reading and Newcastle University, the flood was triggered by a large rock-ice avalanche originating from the Lirung massif, involving glacier ice and rock, which transformed into a highly mobile, long-runout debris flow and generated destructive downstream flooding.

As of 5 October, at least 1,455 people died, 9,287 were injured, and 5,285 were missing in Nepal. Among the missing were 650 foreign nationals from 38 countries. As of 1 October, 112 bodies had been identified.
As of 16 September, 43 people died and 519 were missing in Tibet. Among the missing in Tibet include 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries. This includes 104 Nepali nationals.
Among the missing in Nepal include 189 Indians, 188 Nepali tourists, 65 Americans, 55 Malaysians, 54 Ukrainians, 37 Chinese, 33 Australians, 33 Latvians, 32 British, and 30 Canadians.
The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported nearly 100 Chinese citizens in Nepal missing.

As of 16 September 2026, there were 519 people reported missing in Tibet following the floods.
